text:
A muscle fibre relaxes when its motor neuron stops firing, so acetylcholine is no longer released at the neuromuscular junction and calcium is pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum. The shared note's claim that relaxation happens when the nerve stimulus is too forceful is incorrect: a stronger stimulus causes more contraction, not relaxation. The question is cut off after "when:", so this assumes the standard textbook condition.

CONFIDENCE: 85
